scope: All top-level backing-model structs, enum variants/payloads, and aliases, including nonserialized semantic fields and explicitly classified parser/source helpers. Mapping candidates are not implemented strict-export coverage.

alternative-text-and-tooltips-own-parsed.reason: Alternative text and tooltips own parsed inline content. A scalar metadata string must not flatten formatting or literal protection. A block image may use a scalar attribute only when that is lossless; inline images and icon macros lack upstream node forms.

authored-admonition-form.reason: Retain the actual source form and delimiter. Only delimited forms have an upstream parent-block counterpart; unspecified source provenance is not inferred.

block-id-reftext-promotion-does-not-cove.reason: Block id/reftext promotion does not cover inline anchors, multiple independent IDs, bibliography entry labels, or citation meaning. Reject unsupported forms and content.

candidate.reason: The pinned schema has this representation. This is a mapping inventory, not implemented exporter support; every nested value and semantic control must also be representable.

delimited-admonitions-have-an-upstream-p.reason: Delimited admonitions have an upstream parent-block form. Paragraph admonitions have no corresponding form; do not invent a delimiter or drop their source form. Reject unsupported forms.

derived-catalog.reason: Omit only if supported exported owners preserve everything needed to reconstruct this derived value. Otherwise reject; do not reparse, expand attributes, or register macros during export.

direct-property.reason: Map this semantic property directly only when its owner and every nested value are representable; preserve presence and resolved meaning.

export-already-resolved-meaning-a-remain.reason: Export resolved inline meaning and body text/raw escaping directly. Known block instruction spelling can be omitted after its effects are represented. Reject unknown instructions and remaining raw language operations; never run them during export.

export-the-selected-inline-title-and-its.reason: Export the selected inline title and its presence, not authored attribute syntax or rendered markup.

no-direct-field-mapping-is-established-f.reason: No direct field mapping is established for this property. Strict export must preserve its meaning through an explicitly tested mapping or reject it; do not infer permission to omit it from the outer node shape.

only-an-authored-delimited-form-has-an.reason: Only an authored delimited form has an upstream parent-block counterpart. Reject paragraph form rather than fabricate its delimiter.

ordered-block-prefix-events.reason: Ordered comments and accepted document assignments must become sibling blocks before export. Reject retained prefix events rather than discard them.

parsed-caption-attribution-citation-cont.reason: Parsed caption/attribution/citation content has no dedicated upstream field. A scalar metadata string must not replace formatted or protected inline meaning; reject unsupported content or use an independently named extension.

preserve-constrained-unconstrained-form-.reason: Preserve constrained/unconstrained form without re-reading delimiters.

preserve-line-column-and-each-endpoint-i.reason: Preserve line, column, and each endpoint include chain with the pinned location constraints.

preserve-literal-string-values-and-permi.reason: Preserve literal string values and permitted names. Do not remove semantic quotes, infer arbitrary numbers, or flatten content attributes into this scalar map.

preserve-the-resolved-scalar-value-as-te.reason: Preserve the resolved scalar value as text/raw/character-reference content. Do not apply typography or other language substitutions during export.

preserve-the-resolved-token-order-and-em.reason: Preserve the resolved token order and empty-versus-absent meaning allowed by the schema.

preserve-the-semantic-target-multiple-yo.reason: Preserve the semantic target. Multiple YouTube IDs remain in one comma-separated target; local/remote/data forms must not lose identity or effective media settings.

promote-a-representable-primary-block-an.reason: Promote a representable primary block anchor to id/reftext. Additional or inline anchor identity, bibliography meaning, and independent labels need a lossless mapping or rejection.

promote-the-selected-parsed-reference-la.reason: Promote the selected parsed reference label to block reftext; preserve presence and nested supported inline meaning.

read-retained-positional-slots-directly-.reason: Read retained positional slots directly from the owner, including gaps and explicit empty values; metadata keys $1, $2, and so on are allowed. Native serialization is not the source for these values.

source-state.reason: Parser input, source spelling, or temporary state; omit only after the semantic value and any permitted source coordinates have been preserved.

the-effective-control-remains-semantic-e.reason: The effective control remains semantic even if native JSON omits it. Use a tested lossless mapping to an allowed scalar property when possible; otherwise reject. Do not infer support from the outer node alone.

the-pinned-header-has-title-authors-loca.reason: The pinned header has title/authors/location only. Preserve any authored subtitle, title identity, metadata, or independent presence semantics through a defined representation or reject it.

the-pinned-inline-span-reference-forms-h.reason: The pinned inline span/reference forms have no identity, roles, options, tooltip, or generic attribute map. Reject any unsupported retained control; do not silently drop it.

the-root-attribute-map-cannot-encode-ord.reason: The root attribute map cannot encode ordered body or nested assignments. Preserve this semantic state in a defined representation or reject it.

these-retained-ordered-document-assignme.reason: These retained ordered document assignments affect later nested content. Preserve their source-position semantics or reject; they are not disposable parsing scratch state.

unsupported.reason: No lossless upstream representation is established. Strict export must reject this value, including when nested in otherwise supported content.

upstream-locations-contain-line-column-i.reason: Upstream locations contain line/column/include chain, not byte offsets; preserve the coordinate contract in native data.

use-authored-endpoint-coordinates-omit-a.reason: Use authored endpoint coordinates. Omit an unavailable optional location; reject an unavailable required one. Never fabricate line zero or replace it with line one. Byte offsets are a separate native contract.

use-block-metadata-only-where-the-owning.reason: Use block metadata only where the owning block is representable. Compatible metadata cannot make an unsupported node exportable.

use-effective-semantic-values-and-exact-.reason: Use effective semantic values and exact textual presentation. Root document values allow strings/null; block metadata allows only strings with constrained names. Missing, unset, empty, typed defaults, locks, and ordered assignments are different concerns.

visit-supported-child-inlines-directly-a.reason: Visit supported child inlines directly; a supported child does not make an unsupported span variant valid.

named-basic-table-structure.reason: Strict export rejects table owners. The named profile preserves ordered table/row/cell structure, column widths/alignment/styles, title/caption/metadata, known source spans, positive cell spans and current resolved presentation. Basic export rejects inconsistent span grids and nested AsciiDoc cell scopes. Row/cell ranges are not fabricated; original presentation defaults are edit history, while the current captured value is exported.

core.handling: Supported when every owned value is supported; required titles retain empty presence.

literal-content.handling: Resolved text, references and strong/emphasis/code/mark spans are supported. Verbatim leaves map to text only inside supported literal/listing/verse bodies; other verbatim context, invalid XML references and span controls are rejected.

block-metadata.handling: Supported scalar strings, presence, roles/options, styles, slots and one ordinary identity retain meaning. Unsets, ambiguous values, aliases, bibliography and independent labels are rejected.

document-values.handling: Resolved assignments preserve strings, presence, explicit unsets and numeric spelling. Locks/origins/history are source state after resolution; protected insertion behavior is rejected.

catalogs.handling: Reference and TOC data is omitted only when reconstructible from supported owners. Extra, stale, numbered or bibliography meaning is rejected.

locations.handling: Known line/column endpoints and include chains are preserved. Unknown optional locations are omitted; partial or invalid locations fail. Byte offsets and remap history have no ASG field.

dispatch.handling: Every owner variant is explicitly handled. A rejected owner rejects all of its properties and children without flattening or invented forms.

source-state.handling: Comments and parser routing/edit history can be omitted after resolved values, identity and supported coordinates are preserved. A SafeId cache contributes its effective ID.

pending-content.handling: Unresolved content is rejected; protected document values are not flattened into strings.

substitutions.handling: Resolved block settings are represented by the existing text/raw distinction, inline structure and character references. Body escaping follows formatting spans and explicit reference labels; content attributes and raw fragments retain independent treatment. Omit only resolved instruction spelling. Unknown block stages and remaining raw operations other than one SpecialChars stage are rejected.

decorations.handling: Ordinary unnumbered sections are supported. Nondefault category/numbering, captions, attribution/citation and bibliography labels are rejected on supported owners.

body-assignments.handling: Ordered body assignments and retained assignment events are rejected; they cannot be replaced by the header snapshot.

inline-controls.handling: References reject populated identity, roles/options, scalar controls and tooltips; supported spans reject IDs/roles. Other unsupported macro owners are rejected in full.

unsupported-owners.handling: These owners/payloads have no implemented strict mapping. The entire owning construct is rejected, including empty values and all nested controls/content.

references.handling: Links/URLs/mailto/autolinks preserve targets and effective labels; xrefs retain explicit inline labels or empty automatic labels. Populated metadata, nondefault xref controls and unrepresentable target classification are rejected. UTF-8 target helpers are shared by supported media owners.

lists.handling: Ordered/unordered/callout/description lists preserve marker spelling where retained, item order, terms, principal content, nesting and supported identity/metadata. Levels must follow retained markers. Explicit callout numbers are in markers; auto numbers follow item order. Empty lists, checklists, independent auto numbers, aliases and unsupported nested content are rejected. Inline callout references remain unsupported.

blocks.handling: Retained delimited, paragraph/indented leaf and macro forms preserve bodies, targets, titles and supported metadata. Delimited admonitions preserve their actual opening token. Missing/ambiguous forms, parsed alt/captions, parent paragraph styles, table and STEM bodies require named extensions or explicit errors. Video targets stay complete.

tables.handling: Strict table export rejects the owning table at inner. The named profile maps basic source forms and prepared values without fabricating defaults or flattening cell blocks; inconsistent spans, nested scopes and content retain explicit paths.

content.handling: Preserve resolved caption state and content arrays directly. Titles/reftext retain upstream arrays; reject unsupported nested semantics and stale derived catalogs. Other strict rejection rules remain unchanged.

images.handling: Preserve complete targets, content presence and inline trees, scalar controls, identity, roles/options and node/content locations. Block captions stay separate from inline tooltips. ID-token locations follow the source-only policy. Reject unsupported nested content and ambiguous scalar states; strict image errors remain unchanged.

inline-metadata.handling: Preserve span/reference IDs, ordered role tokens, reference options/scalars and tooltip content directly. Generic highlights remain distinct from marks, including present empty roles. Validate reconstructible inline target registrations and reject duplicates or stale catalogs. ID-token coordinates are source-only; nondefault xref policy and unsupported nested content still fail. Inline metadata excludes block-only fields.

body-attributes.handling: Preserve accepted set/unset events in their existing block sequence, including nested supported bodies, independently from the end-of-header attributes. Preserve scalar presence, literal false and integer spelling; do not replay processing. Reject protected values, rejected/pending parser state and unsupported cell owners. Strict export still rejects ordered body events.

block-forms.handling: Keep paragraph/indented admonition bodies as native blocks and styled parent paragraphs as native inlines. Marked quotes retain their single marker and native blocks. Only real delimited forms carry delimiter; unknown provenance is rejected. Strict export accepts actual delimited admonitions but rejects the additional forms. No synthetic wrappers are introduced.

header.handling: Preserve main title and optional subtitle as separate inline arrays, including present-empty subtitle. Reuse shared metadata/content projection and reconcile header ID and document-top references with the existing combined catalog title. Author/header-attribute reconciliation remains unchanged. Strict header restrictions, independent document-level labels, aliases, stale/duplicate catalogs and unsupported nested content still reject.

checklists.handling: An omitted checked property is an ordinary item; false is unchecked and true is checked. State stays separate from marker, principal and attachments, including nested lists and prepared ordered-list values. Callout items cannot acquire checkboxes. Original checkbox spelling is not retained in the native owner; export does not invent it. Strict export continues to reject checklist state.

tables.handling: Preserve actual delimiter, complete/delimited spans, table sections, column formats, cell block owners and literal context. Optional resolved presentation is a source-position snapshot, distinct from explicit metadata controls. Original edit defaults are not another graph value. Empty/present parts remain distinct. Positive cell spans retain original cell order across sections; inconsistent grids reject. Nested AsciiDoc scopes and initial assignments still reject.
